concepts.title: Sacred Places and Pilgrimage
concepts.definition: Almost every region of India holds sacred places, temples, mosques, churches, gurdwaras, shrines and tirthas, and journeys to them, called pilgrimage, weave the whole land into one sacred geography.
concepts.key_idea: Sacredness is pinned to place: rivers, hills and shrines become doorways of meaning that millions travel to reach.

concepts.title: Sacred Rivers, Mountains and Groves
concepts.definition: Nature itself is revered: the Ganga and other rivers are worshipped as mothers, mountains like Kailash and Govardhan held holy, and trees, plants and sacred groves protected by villages across the land.
concepts.key_idea: Reverence for nature is conservation in cultural dress: a sacred river or grove is guarded by faith, not fences.

concepts.title: The Elements as One Body
concepts.definition: The Bhagavata Purana verse sees ether, air, fire, water, earth, planets, creatures, directions, trees, rivers and seas as organs of the supreme Lord's body, teaching that harming nature is harming the divine itself.
concepts.key_idea: When the world is the body of the sacred, every element deserves respect.

concepts.title: Sharing Across Faiths: Debates and Festivals
concepts.definition: Sacred places grew into meeting grounds: discussions and debates, sharing of goods and experiences, festivals and fairs where communities of every faith met, traded and learned from one another.
concepts.key_idea: Sacred geography is social geography: the same shrine feeds faith, friendship and commerce together.
